safety_verdicts.content: Associated symptoms include a sore throat, blocked ears, and a runny nose.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes runny nose and sore throat but does not document blocked ears as part of the associated symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the symptom of blocked/plugged ears may reduce consideration of otitis media/eustachian tube dysfunction and can affect completeness of the URI symptom picture, but it is unlikely to materially change management in most uncomplicated viral illness cases.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports no unwell contacts and no nausea or vomiting.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not include 'no unwell contacts' and does not document denial of nausea/vomiting.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document “no unwell contacts” and denial of nausea/vomiting removes helpful contextual negatives for infectious risk and alternate diagnoses, but typically results in limited clinical impact beyond reduced diagnostic clarity.

safety_verdicts.content: The impression is a viral upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) with a possible lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI).
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated assessment supports viral URTI/influenza-like illness but does not include the gold qualifier of possible LRTI (/? LRTI).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not recording the qualifier “possible LRTI” may bias the note toward a purely URTI interpretation and could reduce vigilance for evolving chest infection, though the plan already reflects some uncertainty (delayed antibiotics).

safety_verdicts.content: Advised to seek review earlier for worsening symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, or fevers.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not include explicit safety-net advice to seek earlier review for worsening symptoms (e.g., chest pain, worsening SOB, fevers).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting explicit safety-net instructions (seek urgent review for worsening shortness of breath, chest pain, persistent/worsening fevers) can delay escalation in a potentially deteriorating respiratory illness, increasing risk of harm if pneumonia/sepsis or other serious pathology develops.

safety_verdicts.content: No white spots or redness on self-examination; patient did not look
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript: patient did NOT look at the throat, so absence of white spots/redness cannot be asserted. The 'no white spots or redness' portion is unsupported.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Stating there were no white spots/redness despite the patient not examining their throat falsely adds a negative finding, which could inappropriately downplay pharyngitis/tonsillitis severity in downstream decision-making.

safety_verdicts.content: Fevers, chills, and night sweats disrupting sleep
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold explicitly says no fevers; transcript indicates hot/cold/sweaty without measured temperature, not confirmed fever.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting fevers/chills/night sweats as confirmed when the patient only reported feeling hot/cold/sweaty without a measured fever can exaggerate illness severity and may prompt unnecessary antibiotics or investigations.

safety_verdicts.content: Five-day history of dry cough, coryzal symptoms, sore throat, fevers, myalgia, and shortness of breath
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Includes 'fevers' as part of the symptom cluster; gold says no fevers and transcript does not confirm fever (only hot/cold/sweaty without measurement).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Including “fevers” in the symptom cluster when fever is unconfirmed can mischaracterize the clinical syndrome and potentially influence escalation/antibiotic decisions, though it is less likely to directly cause major harm in isolation.
